Comineus, too modest are you, more cruel to your good report than grateful to us that
give you truly.
By your patience, if against yourself you be incensed, will put you, like one that means
his proper harm in manacles, then reason safely with you.
Therefore be it known as to us to all the world that Caius Martius wears this war's
garland, in token of the which my noble steed known to the camp, I give him, with all his
trim belonging.
And from this time, for what he did before Corioles, call him, with all T.H., applause
and clamour of the host, Caius Martius Coriolanus.
